content.title:
Paratroopers from 2nd Battalion The Parachute Regiment and Pathfinders highlighted the high value and unique versatility of airborne forces on the modern battlefield when they jumped into action in a large-scale joint exercise in France. 

Exercise ORION brought together 2,000 soldiers from 16 Air Assault Brigade and 11e Brigade Parachutiste for a nine-day wargame in Brittany. 

First in were British Pathfinders alongside the French Groupe Commando Parachutiste, inserted under freefall parachutes on the St Cyr-Coëtquidan training area. 

They were then joined in jumping by 2PARA Battlegroup, who had taken off from RAF Brize Norton in two A400M Atlas transport aircraft, and two French battlegroups, who were lifted from Orleans-Bricy airbase, near Paris to parachute in. 

A platoon from the Italian Brigata Paracadutisti Folgore also jumped in from Italy. 

Vehicles and stores were also dropped by parachute, including 18 tonnes of rations, ammunition and equipment delivered by an RAF A400M. 

Paratroopers then spread out across the training area to target insurgent forces and establish defensive positions on the enemy’s expected invasion route.

Exercise ORION brought together 2,000 soldiers from 16 Air Assault Brigade and 11e Brigade Parachutiste (11e BP) for a nine-day wargame recently. As the Airborne Combined Joint Force (A-CJF), the two brigades have been trained and ready to deploy together in response to global crises since 2013. Also joining them in Brittany, and demonstrating even greater NATO joint readiness, was a platoon from the Italian Brigata Paracadutisti Folgore, with Ex ORION seeing the joint force tested on a mission to support a NATO ally tackling an insurgency and the threat of invasion. Mike, who made a full recovery from his injuries, has subsequently been taking on various challenges over the years since he left The Parachute Regiment, choosing to raise money for #SUPPORTOURPARAS and his Airborne family.
